title: AI Could Triple Unemployment In Next Decade, Warns Nobel Laureate Daron Acemoglu
source_used: CBS News, 60 Minutes article of 4 Oct 2026 (dl14/c12_cbs.txt), the original behind the NDTV Profit story; NDTV Profit itself returned 403
key_facts: CBS News's 60 Minutes segment (4 Oct 2026) looked at freelancers who train AI models for Mercor and at how AI may affect work.

Mercor, a multibillion-dollar company, has assembled more than 100,000 freelancers who teach AI what they know; AI training is America's fourth-fastest-growing job category on LinkedIn and can pay $20 to $200 an hour.

Nobel Prize-winning economist Daron Acemoglu said 'What we are living through with AI is unprecedented': the first phase of the Industrial Revolution took 80 years, today it is happening in one or two years across many sectors at once.
Acemoglu said that in a worst-case scenario unemployment could triple in the next decade if nothing is done and the US continues on its current course.
He accepted that AI trainers find work but said the number employed in these roles is small relative to the number who will be replaced.
He said companies could design AI to make humans better rather than expendable, or government could use the tax code to reward hiring real people.

Context in the piece: nearly three-fourths of Americans fear AI is coming for jobs (Pew); McKinsey Global Institute's September report says AI could force 11 million US workers into new careers by 2035; Stanford research shows hiring down for young people in the most AI-exposed jobs; US Census research found hiring and wages of recent graduates in AI-exposed majors fell.
NDTV Profit, NDTV, Benzinga and Yahoo Finance repeated the Acemoglu warning on 5 Oct (headlines seen only); the same CBS segment ran in our 5 Oct edition as item 105.
quote_evidence: In a worst-case scenario, unemployment could triple in the next decade, if nothing is done and the U.S. continues on its current course, Acemoglu said.
“What we are living through with AI is unprecedented,” said Acemoglu.

And while Acemoglu acknowledged there will be employment for people training AI, he said, “The number of people they’re employing in these positions is small relative to the number of people who will be replaced.”
why_it_matters_hint: A leading labour economist gives a worst-case scenario for AI and jobs, but says it depends on choices by companies and government.
event_date: 60 Minutes segment aired Sunday 4 Oct 2026; NDTV Profit repeated it on 5 Oct 2026.
notes: Repeat of older news: the NDTV Profit story (5 Oct 10:25Z) relays the CBS News 60 Minutes segment of 4 Oct, which we already carried in our 5 Oct edition as item 105 (same url).
